## Context

An attested gate against a locally present full commit SHA still performs a general fetch before resolving the SHA. In a checkout whose `remote.origin.fetch` maps every head, this becomes `git fetch --no-filter origin`. Git applies the broad refspec and fetches every configured head, including `tickets`, although the gate will materialize one code commit.

The current snapshot contract states that attested mode fetches first when needed and materializes the committed tree at the selected SHA. A locally present full SHA does not need remote freshness. The general fetch adds unrelated transfer cost and can prevent the gate from reaching model execution.

## Rebar-debug orientation

- Step 0(a). Searches for `promisor`, `broad-fetch performance`, `snapshot no-filter partial clone pack bloat`, and the exact timeout found related closed tickets but no bug with this scope. `suave-constant-cow` handles byte-starved transport stalls. `agrologic-oval-bobolink` handles uncoordinated ref updates. Neither limits the ref set of a successful no-filter fetch.
- Step 0(b). The occurrence was reported against `813baac9b01524a024523a8516d563b17f395358`.
- Step 0(c). The F30A worktree matched `origin/main` at that revision.

## Confirmed mechanism

`resolve_ref` calls `fetch_origin` without a target before it attempts `rev_parse`, at `src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py` lines 262 through 266. Materializing callers pass `blobless=False`. `fetch_origin` therefore constructs a general `git fetch --quiet --no-filter origin` and bounds the subprocess at 300 seconds, at `src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py` lines 256 through 283. The configured `remote.origin.fetch` decides which heads that command transfers.

The affected checkout uses `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`. A main-only comparison checkout uses `+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`. The remote currently has 19 heads. The broad checkout contains about 12 GB of Git objects, 115 packs, and recent packs ranging from about 160 MB to 338 MB. One unfinished pack is about 2.3 GB.

## Proof

- F30A completion verification against the full SHA made no model call and failed after the production 300 second fetch timeout. A direct `git fetch origin main` had completed in 3.9 seconds shortly before.
- Ticket `unromantic-ferny-arawana` records an independent run at the same revision. Its broad partial-clone checkout made zero model calls and failed after 512.139 seconds because the general fetch reached the 300 second timeout. Its main-only comparison checkout crossed the fetch boundary and completed with signed PASS in 133.411 seconds.
- The F30A isolated main-only clone also crossed this boundary and completed an attested plan review with signed PASS.
- The target commit tree contains 3,550 objects and zero missing objects in the affected checkout. Materialization did not require a general fetch to acquire this tree.
- Source inspection and process sampling rule out the enrich drain as the direct blocker. Enrich drain releases its advisory lock before model work at `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` lines 358 through 428. It does not own the code snapshot fetch lock.

The configuration differential distinguishes broad ref selection from provider latency, credentials, an absent target object, and the enrich-drain lock. Transport stalls remain possible in general, but they do not explain why the main-only comparison passes while the broad checkout fails at the same revision.

## Defect legitimacy

`docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` states that attested mode fetches first when needed and materializes the selected SHA. It also defines the full SHA as the code version the gate verifies. Fetching unrelated heads is outside that contract and prevents supported gates from completing. This is a defect.

## Remediation constraints

- Preserve freshness for moving branches and tags.
- Preserve targeted recovery for a full SHA that is absent locally.
- Preserve complete blob acquisition for the selected tree.
- Preserve `--end-of-options` protection for client-supplied refs.
- Do not narrow or rewrite the checkout owner's configured refspec as a side effect.
- Keep attested mode fail-closed when the selected ref or required object cannot be obtained.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A locally resolvable full SHA does not trigger a general fetch whose scope expands through `remote.origin.fetch`.
- [x] A moving branch or tag is refreshed before resolution.
- [x] A missing full SHA uses a targeted fetch and either resolves or fails closed with an actionable error.
- [x] Materialization acquires every missing blob for the selected tree without fetching unrelated heads.
- [x] A deterministic local-remote test uses a broad refspec and a large unrelated branch, then proves that resolving and materializing a present SHA does not transfer the unrelated objects.
- [x] Existing snapshot security, partial-clone, timeout, and concurrency tests remain green.
- [x] Current snapshot documentation describes fetch scope for full SHAs, moving refs, and missing objects.
- [x] Focused tests, `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the project test gate pass.
